title: Quietest time to visit Dubrovnik (and how to dodge the cruise crowds)
author: Brogan
intro: Late October and April are the sweet spots for Dubrovnik: warm enough to enjoy, without the summer crush. Whenever you go, the cruise ship timetable matters more than the month.
seo_title: Quietest time to visit Dubrovnik: April and late October
seo_description: April, May and late October are quietest while still warm. November to March is emptiest but many places close. Plus how to dodge cruise days.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Best balance:** April, May, late Oct
- **Quietest of all:** November to March
- **Busiest:** July and August
- **Biggest factor:** cruise ship days

Dubrovnik's walled old town is small, so a few thousand extra people make a huge difference. Picking the right month helps, but checking which days cruise ships are in port helps even more.

sections.heading: Month by month
sections.text:
| Months | Typical high | Crowds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| November to March | 12 to 17°C | Quietest, but many places closed |
| April | About 18°C | Quiet, spring |
| May and June | 23 to 27°C | Busy, but warm sea |
| July and August | About 30°C | Busiest and hottest |
| September | About 26°C | Busy, warm sea |
| October | About 21°C | Getting quieter |

The temperatures are from our [Dubrovnik guide](/destinations/dubrovnik). For most people, the best trade-off is either side of summer: April and early May, or the second half of October.

sections.heading: Why cruise days matter
sections.text:
Dubrovnik has been one of the Mediterranean's best-known overtourism stories, and cruise ships are a big part of that. On a busy summer day, thousands of passengers come ashore at Gruž port and head for the old town at once.

The city now limits cruise traffic, generally to two ships a day at the main port, with a target of around 8,000 passengers on the busiest days, but those limits aren't absolute and some days still go over. Cruise passengers usually arrive mid-morning and leave by late afternoon.

Tip: look up the cruise timetable for your dates before you plan your days. On days with two or more ships, do the city walls and the main street, the Stradun, before 9am or after 5pm, and spend the middle of the day on Lokrum island or a beach.

sections.heading: Winter: quietest, with catches
sections.text:
From November to March, Dubrovnik is very quiet. You can walk the Stradun almost alone, and hotel prices fall a long way.

- **Many places close:** a lot of restaurants, beach bars and some hotels shut for the season.
- **Fewer flights:** some UK routes are summer only, so you may need to change planes.
- **Rain:** November and December are among the wettest months.
- **Boats:** island ferries and boat trips run less often.

For a calm city break in winter, it can still be lovely, especially in December, when the old town has a small Christmas market and lights.

sections.heading: Spring and autumn: the sweet spots
sections.text:
April is quiet and green, with highs around 18°C: good for walking the walls and exploring, though too cool for most people to swim. May is warmer and busier, and the sea starts to warm up.

October is often the best month of all. The sea is still warm from the summer, highs are around 21°C, and once the school holidays are over, the crowds drop week by week.

Watch out: Easter, the late-May bank holiday and the October half term bring extra visitors from the UK. If you can go outside those weeks, you'll notice the difference.

sections.heading: Walking the city walls
sections.text:
The walls are the highlight of most trips, and the place where crowds and heat matter most. They run for about 2km around the old town, and walking the full circuit takes one to two hours, with plenty of steps and very little shade.

- **Go early:** the first hour after opening is the coolest and calmest.
- **Bring water and a hat:** in July and August, the stone radiates heat by late morning.
- **Walk anticlockwise from Pile Gate** if you want the steepest climb, to the Minčeta Tower, out of the way first.

Out of season, the walls have shorter opening hours, so check the times before you plan your day.

sections.heading: Other ways to avoid the crowds
sections.text:
- **Stay outside the old town:** in Lapad or Ploče, and come in early and late.
- **Walk the walls first thing:** they open early in summer, before the heat and the tours.
- **Take a day trip:** [Kotor](/destinations/kotor) in Montenegro, the island of [Korčula](/destinations/korcula) or the town of Cavtat.
- **Look at quieter swaps:** our [alternatives to Dubrovnik](/blog/alternatives-to-dubrovnik) post suggests places with the same feel.

If you'd rather have a bigger base on the coast, [Split](/destinations/split) has more going on in the evenings and more ferry links to the islands.

sections.heading: Still deciding?
sections.text: For more of the coast, see our [Croatia](/destinations/holidays-in-croatia) page. And if you're weighing up a few quieter trips, our posts on the [quietest time to visit Venice](/blog/quietest-time-to-visit-venice) and [Amsterdam](/blog/quietest-time-to-visit-amsterdam) use the same approach. If you can't agree where to go, add them to [somewhere.party](/) and let the draw decide.

faqs.question: What is the quietest month to visit Dubrovnik?
faqs.answer: January and February are the quietest, but many places close. For warm weather with fewer crowds, April and the second half of October are best.

faqs.question: How do you avoid cruise ship crowds in Dubrovnik?
faqs.answer: Check the cruise timetable for your dates, and visit the old town and walls before 9am or after 5pm on days with ships in port.

faqs.question: Is Dubrovnik worth visiting in winter?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a quiet city break, but expect closed restaurants, fewer flights and more rain. It's not a beach destination in winter.

faqs.question: Is October a good time to visit Dubrovnik?
faqs.answer: Yes. The sea is still warm, highs are around 21°C, and crowds fall away after the school holidays.
